assistant_messages.content:
Our invoice approval process is:

- Accounts Payable (AP) receives and logs the invoice.
- AP performs a three-way match against the purchase order and goods receipt note.
- If the invoice does not match, it is rejected and returned to the supplier for correction and resubmission.
- If it matches, the budget holder approves it within five working days.
- Invoices above **€10,000** also require Finance Controller sign-off.
- AP schedules approved invoices for the next weekly payment run.
- Treasury releases payment on Thursday.
- The invoice, purchase order, and approvals are archived for seven years.
- Late approvals trigger an AP reminder; after a second reminder, the issue is escalated to the Head of Finance. [1][2][3]

The diagram shows the main approval path, the rejection/resubmission loop, the €10,000 escalation point, and the delayed-approval escalation. Source: **292-invoice-approval-policy.md** — Invoice Approval Policy.

- Accounts Payable (AP) receives and logs the invoice.
- AP performs a three-way match against the purchase order and goods receipt note.
- If the invoice does not match, it is rejected and returned to the supplier for correction and resubmission.
- If it matches, the budget holder approves it within five working days.
- Invoices above **€10,000** also require Finance Controller sign-off.
- AP schedules approved invoices for the next weekly payment run.
- Treasury releases payment on Thursday.
- The invoice, purchase order, and approvals are archived for seven years.
- Late approvals trigger an AP reminder; after a second reminder, the issue is escalated to the Head of Finance. [1][2][3]
